60: public class HandleHelper extends JavacAnnotationHandler<Helper> {
61: 	private List<JCStatement> getStatementsFromJcNode(JCTree tree) {

63: 		if (tree instanceof JCCase) return ((JCCase) tree).stats;

67: 	private void setStatementsOfJcNode(JCTree tree, List<JCStatement> statements) {
68: 		if (tree instanceof JCBlock) ((JCBlock) tree).stats = statements;
69: 		else if (tree instanceof JCCase) ((JCCase) tree).stats = statements;
70: 		else throw new IllegalArgumentException("Can't set statements on node type: " + tree.getClass());
71: 	}

74: 		handleExperimentalFlagUsage(annotationNode, ConfigurationKeys.HELPER_FLAG_USAGE, "@Helper");
75: 		
76: 		deleteAnnotationIfNeccessary(annotationNode, Helper.class);
77: 		JavacNode annotatedType = annotationNode.up();
78: 		JavacNode containingBlock = annotatedType == null ? null : annotatedType.directUp();
79: 		List<JCStatement> origStatements = getStatementsFromJcNode(containingBlock == null ? null : containingBlock.get());
80: 		
81: 		if (annotatedType == null || annotatedType.getKind() != Kind.TYPE || origStatements == null) {
82: 			annotationNode.addError("@Helper is legal only on method-local classes.");
83: 			return;
84: 		}
85: 		
86: 		JCClassDecl annotatedType_ = (JCClassDecl) annotatedType.get();
87: 		Iterator<JCStatement> it = origStatements.iterator();
88: 		while (it.hasNext()) {
89: 			if (it.next() == annotatedType_) {

91: 			}
92: 		}

98: 			String n = ch.getName();
99: 			if (n == null || n.isEmpty() || n.charAt(0) == '<') continue;
100: 			knownMethodNames.add(n);
101: 		}
102: 		
103: 		Collections.sort(knownMethodNames);
104: 		final String[] knownMethodNames_ = knownMethodNames.toArray(new String[0]);
105: 		
106: 		final Name helperName = annotationNode.toName("$" + annotatedType_.name);
107: 		final boolean[] helperUsed = new boolean[1];
108: 		final JavacTreeMaker maker = annotationNode.getTreeMaker();
109: 		
110: 		TreeVisitor<Void, Void> visitor = new TreeScanner<Void, Void>() {
111: 			@Override public Void visitMethodInvocation(MethodInvocationTree node, Void p) {
112: 				JCMethodInvocation jcmi = (JCMethodInvocation) node;
113: 				apply(jcmi);
114: 				return super.visitMethodInvocation(node, p);
115: 			}

117: 			private void apply(JCMethodInvocation jcmi) {
118: 				if (!(jcmi.meth instanceof JCIdent)) return;
119: 				JCIdent jci = (JCIdent) jcmi.meth;
120: 				if (Arrays.binarySearch(knownMethodNames_, jci.name.toString()) < 0) return;
121: 				jcmi.meth = maker.Select(maker.Ident(helperName), jci.name);
122: 				recursiveSetGeneratedBy(jcmi.meth, annotationNode);
123: 				helperUsed[0] = true;
124: 			}
125: 		};
126: 		
127: 		while (it.hasNext()) {
128: 			JCStatement stat = it.next();
129: 			stat.accept(visitor, null);
130: 		}
131: 		
132: 		if (!helperUsed[0]) {
133: 			annotationNode.addWarning("No methods of this helper class are ever used.");
134: 			return;
135: 		}
136: 		
137: 		ListBuffer<JCStatement> newStatements = new ListBuffer<JCStatement>();
138: 		
139: 		boolean mark = false;
140: 		for (JCStatement stat : origStatements) {
141: 			newStatements.append(stat);

part.text: The javac handler only handles `JCBlock`/`JCCase` as containing nodes, but when a local class is directly in a method body, the direct parent in the Lombok AST is the method node. Let me check how the javac AST structures method bodies.

state.title: JCBlock|buildMethod|buildStatement|stats

part.text: The JavacAST flattens method bodies: `buildMethod` adds `method.body.stats` statements as direct children of the method node (src/core/lombok/javac/JavacAST.java:452-458). So when a local class is directly in a method body, `directUp()` is the `JCMethodDecl`. `HandleCleanup` already handles this pattern (see src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleCleanup.java:91-96). The eclipse handler already handles `AbstractMethodDeclaration`, so only the javac handler needs fixing.

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleHelper.java: when a `@Helper`-annotated local class sits directly in a method body, the JavacAST makes the statements of `method.body.stats` direct children of the method node, so `directUp()` returns the `JCMethodDecl`, which the handler didn't recognize — only `JCBlock`/`JCCase`.

The fix adds `JCMethodDecl` support to `getStatementsFromJcNode`/`setStatementsOfJcNode` (mirroring the existing pattern in `HandleCleanup`); the eclipse handler already supported `AbstractMethodDeclaration`.

Verification: `ant test.instance` runs all 391 transform tests — both `javac-HelperInMethod.java` (the failing case: helper class directly in a method body) and `javac-HelperInInitializationBlock.java` now pass, with 0 failures overall.
